walkthroughs.body_html:
Atomic Structure HL — a core area of Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Atomic Structure HL brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Atomic Structure HL.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Mendeleev

mcqs.q: In a standard hydrogen electrode used as a reference, what is the assigned electrode potential?
options: The standard hydrogen electrode actually has zero potential because hydrogen has no charge.
The standard hydrogen electrode has a potential of -1 V to balance copper at +1 V.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
Exactly 0 V by convention — all other electrode potentials are measured relative to it.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
The standard hydrogen electrode has a potential of -1 V to balance copper at +1 V.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.

mcqs.q: What is the role of the fingerprint region (below ~1500 cm^-1) in IR spectroscopy?
options: The fingerprint region is the part that contains all the most useful absorptions.
The fingerprint region is used to identify which functional groups are present.
It is unique to each compound — used to identify a specific molecule by matching to a known spectrum.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.

sequence.def: The sample is turned into a gas
Electron bombardment knocks out electrons, making + ions
An electric field speeds the ions up
A magnetic field bends paths by mass-to-charge ratio
Ions are counted to build the mass spectrum
